findings.title: Date-override end check compares Dayjs objects by identity
findings.body: `dayjs(date.start).add(...) === dayjs(date.end).add(...)` compares two freshly created Dayjs object references, so it is always false and the zero-length override branch never triggers. It should use `.isSame(...)`. As written, a zero-length override (start equals end) is not handled as intended.

findings.title: Slot inside a date override skips the busy-time check entirely
findings.body: When a date override exists for the slot's day and the slot falls inside it, `checkIfIsAvailable` returns true right away (`if (dateOverrideExist) return true;`). That bypasses the `busy` check at the end of the function. A fixed host with a date override who already has a calendar event or booking at that time will still be reported as available. This is the exact problem the PR is meant to fix (round-robin events booked while fixed hosts are unavailable), so the fix is incomplete.

findings.title: Working-hours check uses the slot start for both start and end
findings.body: `end` is computed from `slotStartTime` instead of the slot end time, so `end > workingHour.endTime` is effectively checking the start again. A slot that runs past the end of working hours is not rejected. Also, `workingHours.find` returns true when any single working-hours block excludes the slot, so a slot inside a later block (e.g. 14:00-18:00 when there is also a 09:00-12:00 block) is rejected. The check should ask whether the slot fits inside at least one block (`.some` with start >= startTime and end <= endTime).

findings.title: Working-hours rejection logic inverted for multiple availability blocks
findings.body: The predicate `start < workingHour.startTime || end > workingHour.endTime` is true whenever the slot is outside one particular block. Since `.find` is used, any non-matching block causes the whole slot to be rejected, even when another block contains it. Users with split working hours (for example a lunch break) will see valid slots removed.

findings.title: Override timezone may be undefined, falling back to server timezone
findings.body: `dayjs(...).tz(override.timeZone)` is called without guaranteeing `override.timeZone` is set. The timeZone is copied from `availability.timeZone` in slots.ts, which may be missing. dayjs `.tz(undefined)` then uses the process's local timezone, so the computed offset depends on the server's TZ setting rather than the organizer's. The overrides' timezone should be validated or defaulted to the organizer timezone.

findings.title: New timezone test would pass without the fix
findings.body: The added assertion uses the +6:00 timezone and expects the same UTC slots (08:30-11:30Z) as the +5:30 case. Slot times are returned as UTC ISO strings, so this output is independent of the invitee timezone, and the old `getUTCHours` code would produce the same result. The test does not check that a date override adapts to a different timezone. There is also no test for the main fix: a round-robin event where a fixed host's date override must respect that host's busy times.
